faqs.question: What do you put in a boo basket for adults?
faqs.answer: Fill six slots: a container, one snack, one cosy item such as socks or a throw, one spooky item such as a ghost candle or a horror film, one personal item tied to a shared memory, and a note. Adults notice quality more than quantity, so spend on one good cosy item rather than three cheap ones.

faqs.question: What does 'you've been booed' mean?
faqs.answer: It means someone left an anonymous Halloween basket on your doorstep as part of a neighbourhood game. The traditional version asks you to pass it on to another neighbour; the modern boo basket is usually personal and has no chain.

faqs.question: When should you give a boo basket?
faqs.answer: Any time between 1 October and Halloween night on 31 October. Giving it early in October means the cosy and spooky items get used for the whole season, and shopping before mid-October avoids picked-over shelves.

faqs.question: How much should a boo basket cost?
faqs.answer: Anywhere from about $20 to $75 by our estimate of US shop prices. At $20 you can fill all six slots with discount-store items; at $75 the same six slots get better materials, not more items.

faqs.question: Are boo baskets only for kids?
faqs.answer: No. The trend took off with parents, but couples and best friends now make them too. Swap the toys for a cosy item, a grown-up treat and a personal note and it works for any age.

faqs.question: What are some cheap boo basket fillers?
faqs.answer: A plastic pumpkin pail, fun-size candy, fuzzy socks, glow sticks and a printed photo together come to roughly $15–20 at US discount stores. A handwritten note costs almost nothing and is usually the part people keep.

faqs.question: Can I put homemade treats in a boo basket?
faqs.answer: Only if you know the recipient's allergies. FDA guidance is to give commercially wrapped treats and to keep home-baked goods away from a child with a food allergy, so for neighbours or children you do not know well, stick to sealed, labelled food or skip food entirely.

faqs.question: What can I use instead of a basket?
faqs.answer: A plastic pumpkin pail, a popcorn bowl, a tote bag, a plant pot or a lidded crate all work. Pick a container they will reuse after Halloween so the packaging is part of the gift.

faqs.question: How do you send a boo basket to someone far away?
faqs.answer: Post a small, flat parcel early, with socks, tea bags, a photo and a card, and keep food sealed and labelled for transit. Then send a link they open on the day, so the moment still lands on Halloween even if the parcel arrives early.

faqs.question: What should the note in a boo basket say?
faqs.answer: Two or three specific sentences about the person, such as something they did this year that you noticed, or a memory from a past October. Avoid a note that only says Happy Halloween; the basket already says that.

article.contentMarkdown:
# Boo Basket Ideas: What to Put Inside, Sorted by Budget

The boo basket ideas that work follow one formula: a container, one snack, one cosy item, one spooky item, one personal item and a note. Fill those six slots and the basket feels complete at $20; spend $75 and each slot gets an upgrade, but the note is still the part people keep. That is why we suggest making the note a link they can reopen: a page created on SubhSandesh is viewed 11.1 times on average, and 48.3% of those views happen on a phone, where a card's link gets tapped.

Below: the trend's origin, the six slots, filler checklists at three budgets, ideas per recipient, allergy rules and delivery. Prices are our estimates unless a source is linked.

## What is a boo basket, and where did the trend come from?

A boo basket is a container of small Halloween-themed treats and gifts, given to someone in the weeks before 31 October. It grew out of an older neighbourhood game called "You've Been Booed", in which a basket was left anonymously on a doorstep with a note asking the recipient to pass the game on.

[NBC 7 San Diego's 2026 explainer](https://www.nbcsandiego.com/holidays/boo-baskets-halloween-trend/4081809/) draws the line clearly: the traditional booed basket is anonymous and expects the chain to continue, while a modern boo basket can be completely personal, with no chain at all. Either works: leave it anonymously on a porch, or hand it to someone you know.

[The Independent counted over 82,000 TikTok videos tagged #boobasket in October 2024](https://www.the-independent.com/life-style/boo-baskets-tiktok-halloween-trend-b2637986.html), and reported a backlash among parents who saw lavish baskets as "needless consumerism". The lesson: it does not need to be expensive to land.

## The 6-slot anatomy of a good boo basket

Each slot: its job, a typical spend, a pick, and the mistake to avoid. Spends are our estimates from typical US shop shelves, not survey data.

### 1. The container

It sets the theme before anything is unwrapped. A plastic pumpkin pail costs about $1–3, a woven basket $8–12, a lidded wooden crate $15 or more. Pick something reusable, such as a tote, a popcorn bowl or a plant pot; avoid a container so big that six items look sparse.

### 2. The snack

This is the treat eaten on day one. Fun-size candy runs about $4–6 a bag; a caramel apple kit or gourmet popcorn $6–10. Pick their actual favourite, not the most photogenic sweet; avoid anything homemade unless you know their allergy status.

### 3. The cosy item

October gifts lean warm. Fuzzy socks cost $3–6, a mug with cocoa sachets $8–12, a small throw blanket $15–25. Pick one cosy item and make it a good one; avoid stacking three cheap ones; they read as filler.

### 4. The spooky item

This slot makes it a boo basket. Glow sticks or a ghost candle cost $2–10; a horror film, ghost-story collection or tarot deck $10–20. Pick something useful after 31 October; avoid decorations they must find a shelf for.

### 5. The personal item

Only you can fill this slot. A printed photo strip costs about $1, an engraved keyring $10–15, and a playlist written on a card takes a few minutes. Pick something tied to a shared memory; avoid generic "for him" or "for her" items.

### 6. The note

The note is what they reread. A handwritten card costs $1–5, and a link on it can point to a page you made in about five minutes. Write two or three specific sentences; avoid a note that only says "Happy Halloween"; the basket already says that.

## Boo basket fillers at $20, $40 and $75

Every price is our estimate for US shops in October; treat totals as a planning range, not a quote. The jump to $75 buys better materials, not more items.

The $20 basket (about $16–20):

- Plastic pumpkin pail ($2) and orange tissue paper ($1)
- A bag of their favourite fun-size candy ($5)
- Fuzzy Halloween socks ($4)
- Glow sticks or a mini skeleton ($3)
- A printed photo of you both ($1) and a handwritten card ($2)

The $40 basket (about $35–40):

- Woven basket with a handle ($10)
- Gourmet popcorn or a caramel apple kit ($7)
- A Halloween mug with two cocoa sachets ($9)
- A ghost-shaped candle or a scary paperback ($8)
- A photo strip and a card carrying your link ($3)

The $75 basket (about $65–75):

- Lidded wooden crate or lined tote ($15)
- Bakery treats, commercially packed and labelled ($12)
- A small knit throw blanket ($20)
- A horror film on disc, a board game or a tarot deck ($15)
- An engraved keyring or framed photo, plus the card ($10)

## Boo basket ideas by recipient: 3 for each of 5 people

For a boyfriend or husband:

- His favourite sour sweets, horror-film socks and a handwritten "movie night owed" ticket
- Hot sauce in a skull bottle, pumpkin-spice coffee and a photo from your first October together
- A retro horror DVD, microwave popcorn and a card listing three things you like about him

For a girlfriend or wife:

- A ghost candle, a face mask and a letter naming one thing she did this year that you noticed
- A mini pumpkin, paints and a print of your favourite photo of her
- A cosy throw, her favourite chocolate and a "date night at home" plan written as a ticket

For a best friend:

- Two matching mugs, cocoa and a photo of your worst-ever costume
- A ghost-story book, a bookmark and a note guessing which story they will hate most
- Nail stickers, a horror-film list you both must finish and their favourite snack

For kids:

- Halloween pyjamas, a glow-in-the-dark book and stickers
- A pumpkin-carving kit with child-safe tools and one wrapped treat
- Bubbles, chalk and a small plush ghost, with no sugar at all

For someone far away:

- A flat parcel of socks, tea bags, a photo and a card
- A small parcel posted early, plus a link they open on the day
- A video call where you each open the basket the other built

## Food safety: 9 allergens and 3 rules for edible fillers

The [US Food and Drug Administration's Halloween safety tips](https://www.fda.gov/food/buy-store-serve-safe-food/halloween-food-safety-tips-parents) say to give commercially wrapped treats, to check wrappers for pinholes or tears, and to keep home-baked goods away from a child with a food allergy. For very young children, the same page says to remove choking hazards such as gum, peanuts, hard sweets and small toys.

Read labels for the allergens that matter. The [FDA's food allergy page](https://www.fda.gov/food/nutrition-food-labeling-and-critical-foods/food-allergies) lists nine major US allergens: milk, eggs, fish, crustacean shellfish, tree nuts, peanuts, wheat, soybeans and sesame, with sesame added from 1 January 2023. If you do not know what the recipient avoids, ask or leave food out.

Non-food baskets are a complete answer, not a compromise. [FARE's Teal Pumpkin Project](https://www.foodallergy.org/our-initiatives/awareness-campaigns/living-teal/teal-pumpkin-project), adopted nationally in 2014, exists so children with food allergies get non-food treats at Halloween.

## How to deliver a boo basket without spoiling it

Most baskets are handed over between 1 October and Halloween night, and the surprise matters less to the recipient than you think. In a 2026 Behavioral Sciences paper, [Puente-Díaz and Cavazos-Arroyo found that people assigned the giver's role rated surprise as more important than people assigned the recipient's role](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13603195/), and that this gap explained why givers valued creative gifts more. Their second experiment replicated it with 281 people.

So a ring-and-run is optional; a doorstep basket plus a "check your porch" text works. Spend the effort on the six slots.

Plan the timing, though. We have no Halloween data, but on Raksha Bandhan, the nearest festival we measure, 49.4% of greeting pages (n = 89) were built on the festival day itself. Shop by mid-October, before the good fillers sell out.

For the note slot, we built a [Halloween card they play through](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween). You add their name, a letter, up to six photos and a word to carve on the pumpkin.

They knock three times, carve a jack-o'-lantern until your word glows, read your letter by flashlight and answer "Will you be my boo?", and you get an email the first time they answer. It has partner, bestie, family and kids modes, and ends in a Boo License sized for an Instagram Story.

| Note option | What it takes | Can they replay it? | What we can measure |
|---|---|---|---|
| Handwritten card | $1–5 and a pen | Yes, if kept | Nothing: paper is not tracked |
| Printed photo with a line on the back | About $1 at a print kiosk | Yes, if kept | Nothing: paper is not tracked |
| Card with a link to a Halloween page | About 5 minutes to build | Yes, in any browser | 11.1 views per created page; 48.3% on a phone |
| Card with a link to the premium page | About 10 minutes to build | Yes, in any browser | Same platform averages; no Halloween-only data yet |

A link gets reopened, which a paper note cannot promise. If you want a voice note, the [premium Halloween page](https://subhsandesh.in/happy-halloween-premium) adds one up to 60 seconds, up to 12 photos and an optional unlock time, so the link shows only their name and a countdown until the moment you choose.

## When a boo basket, or our page, is the wrong choice

A boo basket is wrong for someone who finds gifts awkward, and for a neighbour you have never spoken to if a chain note would feel like an obligation. The Independent's 2024 report on parents' backlash is a fair warning: a basket that feels like a performance can land as pressure.

Our page has limits too: it is a one-person greeting, not a party invitation, and its screens are English only. It needs a screen (48.3% of views are on a phone), so a recipient who rarely uses screens is better served by paper. For a small child, a physical toy usually beats any screen, even with the kids mode's no-scares tone.

## Sources

- NBC 7 San Diego, "Boo baskets are having a moment", 2 October 2026
- The Independent, "What are 'boo baskets'?", 30 October 2024
- Puente-Díaz and Cavazos-Arroyo, "Asymmetries in Gift-Exchange", Behavioral Sciences, 2026
- US Food and Drug Administration, "Halloween Food Safety Tips for Parents", current as of 5 March 2024
- US Food and Drug Administration, "Food Allergies", current as of 11 March 2026
- Food Allergy Research & Education, "Teal Pumpkin Project", no publication date stated
